description: Outages of up to 12 hours a day. With additional fuel and purchased Israeli electricity, supply ran 10-15 hours a day depending on demand after October 2018, against 5-7 hours before it.
energy_note: Five hours of power a day, in living memory.

aspect: It cascades into the water supply
description: Pumping, treatment and desalination all need power, so an electricity deficit is also a water deficit and a sanitation deficit. OCHA linked increased electricity supply directly to improved water access.
energy_note: No power, therefore no water, therefore no sanitation.

aspect: Household life is rebuilt around the schedule
description: Laundry, baking, charging, homework and pumping all happen in the window. Missing the window means the task waits a day, and the person doing the waiting is whoever runs the house.
energy_note: Doing the washing at 2am because that's when it's on.

aspect: Refrigeration failure is a food and medicine cost
description: Insulin, vaccines and food all need a cold chain. Intermittent power means spoilage that is paid for repeatedly by households with no margin.
energy_note: Throwing away food you couldn't afford, again.

aspect: And it ends the possibility of most kinds of work
description: No manufacturing, no reliable remote work, no data centre, no cold storage business. The power schedule sets a ceiling on what industries can exist.
energy_note: Whole industries, ruled out by a generator.

aspect: EXAMPLE - five to seven hours a day
description: Before October 2018 Gaza had 5-7 hours of electricity a day; additional fuel for the power plant and purchased Israeli electricity raised it to 10-15 hours depending on demand, against outages of up to 12 hours at other periods.
energy_note: Five hours of power a day, as a normal year.
